tss_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
outstanding: Conflict (included by default): The sources disagree on both characterisation and extent. (a) NGA Pub. 148 says the Panama Canal VTMS covers the approaches to Colón, which on a plain reading includes the IMO 'approaches to Puerto Cristobal' TSS. NGA is the same volume type relied on for the Chilean VTS links. (b) ACP's own texts call the unit a signal station, not a VTS, and give no service area. They define the Canal operating areas as the Atlantic entrance and its anchorage areas; the outer anchorage and sea buoy end at 9°26'20"N, 1.7-5 nm south of the TSS's inner ends. (c) The ACP mandatory call point (8 nm from the breakwater in N-2-2026, against 6 miles in the Navigation Regulation art. 36 and 12 miles in NGA) falls on the inner end of the TSS, within the imprecision of an 'Atlantic Breakwater' reference whose two heads are 0.3 nm apart. So whether ACP traffic control reaches the TSS depends on which of these readings is taken. Official sources support either reading, so decision 7 applies. Classed as Supplemental (traffic control, not a formal VTS), with coverage limited to the inner end. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. No ACP statement of VTMS radar/AIS coverage or a service polygon was found. The official Acuerdo 360 text on pancanal.com is a scanned image and could not be read (no OCR available); the compiled regulation copy is a third-party host and may predate recent amendments. ACP N-1-2026 was not retrieved. The same reasoning should be applied to TSS-0176 (Flamenco Signal Station, Pacific entrance) for consistency; that TSS was not re-examined here.
